study type: linked facility and population-based cross-sectional survey
exposure: Availability of electronic Health Information System (HIS) tools
outcome: Health Information System (HIS) data quality and use indicators
cohort: The study included 3,016 mothers for the population-based survey and 81 health posts, 71 health centers, and 15 hospitals for the facility survey.
finding: Maternal service indicators showed promising performance, but current Health Information System (HIS) performance was suboptimal, and both service user (maternal education, wealth, distance) and HIS-related factors (availability of electronic HIS tools) were associated with maternal service uptake.
